planned_arguments.prompt:
Edit the first supplied image, my own initial flat poster. The second supplied image is the mandatory exact lamp identity reference. Create one revised flat opaque landscape 16:9 poster, keeping the photographic light-and-folded-paper montage genre.

Observed issues to correct: at 720px width the long description is a tiny single line, and every text group is stacked in one right-side information column on a blank lit plane. The photo still reads as a single staged product scene. Reorganise the actual image editing and text relationships together; enlarge the body and give both description sentences a coherent natural multiline paragraph. Preserve the accurate complete forest-green product, all required copy once, warm desk illumination and the crisp material detail.

Build a decisive PHOTO MONTAGE of three related exposures at different scales, with hard oblique photographic crop boundaries across the full frame. A complete product photograph occupies the left-centre, clearly separated from an enlarged crop of its glowing underside and from a very large warm-lit folded-paper close-up. Abrupt changes of scale, lighting and edge direction identify photographic editing, rather than one room or tabletop backdrop. The complete lamp crosses one crop intersection without being sliced or duplicated; its whole wide curved horizontal shade, TWO connected straight supports and oval base are visible once with deep forest-green identity unchanged. Keep its supporting surface only where needed for credible base contact and warm desk light. The other areas are tightly cropped subject surfaces showing paper thickness, ridge depth and changing warm light, not empty background walls for information. A strongly illuminated diagonal fold runs toward and across the middle of the poster, connecting the lamp shade to the reading route. The body sits on the stable, evenly lit portion adjacent to that fold, with sufficient contrast and no letters across a shadow seam. Deep-green paper macro shapes and warm ivory light crops construct the outer frame and scale tension; no generic abstract decoration.

Shift the title to a moderate two-line second anchor near the lamp base/crossing crop in the lower-left, with the English line adjacent. The complete lamp's light and the rising fold edge lead FIRST to the two contiguous description sentences in the upper/middle-right, large enough for easy reading at width720. Use a mature medium-weight humanist Korean/Latin sans with coherent syllables, balanced apertures, normal width and word spaces, stable horizontal baseline, and no artificial slant in the body. For the second long description use two or three phrase-length horizontal lines; do not squeeze it into one line. Aim at approximately 13–14px body glyph height at the 720px usage view, and give the paragraph enough room. Preserve all punctuation. The title can have a restrained oblique sans treatment while its syllables remain clear, but do not let it displace body content.

Below the description, follow the shared optical start and the same continuous illuminated fold edge into two adjoining functional groups: event/date/time/place together; admission/visit together next to it. Keep the next group close enough to find naturally, with a shared baseline and distinct but modest spacing. Continue into the invitation sentence and intact URL below those groups, on the same connected reading plane. This should form a broad, readable route across the photographic intersection rather than one tall detached panel or tiny footer. No new labels, bullets, rules, arrows or print. The photo editing must determine these positions. Respect meaningful word spaces and natural wrapping; no rotated text, one-syllable orphan lines or expanded tracking to fill a line.

Maintain a commercially useful product experience invitation. No actual release facts, invented specifications, company logo, QR, watermark or extra copy. Exclude passive solid/near-solid/split-colour headline/date/info templates with subordinate product pictures, and exclude empty indoor planes made to hold title blocks. No frame, room mockup, sheet of alternatives or multi-poster panel. One finished poster only.
